state_feedback.announce_after_inquiry: Avoid moving to Announce after inquiry before all concerns are mirrored.
state_feedback.announce_after_inquiry_tip: Keep it brief and invite input (e.g., 'How does that sound?').
state_feedback.closure_followup_without_literature: You have a follow-up plan; offer some information to review at home so they can come back with specific questions.
state_feedback.closure_literature_without_followup: You offered take-home information; also book a follow-up so they know when they can bring questions back.
state_feedback.neutral_framing_tip: Keep framing neutral and open; invite questions.
state_feedback.secure_before_inquire: Ask one open concern question before offering reassurance.
state_feedback.secure_before_inquire_after_question: You asked an open question, then moved into reassurance before giving them space to answer.
state_feedback.secure_before_inquire_after_question_tip: After asking what's on their mind, pause before offering reassurance.
state_feedback.secure_before_inquire_reason: You moved into reassurance before asking about their concerns - try an open question first
state_feedback.secure_before_inquire_tip: Ask what's on their mind (e.g., 'What are your thoughts about the vaccines we discussed?') before offering reassurance.
state_feedback.secure_before_mirror: Mirror the active concern{topic_hint} before offering more education.
state_feedback.secure_before_mirror_analytical_reason: You're educating before mirroring - try validating their reasoning first; this person values having their logic acknowledged
state_feedback.secure_before_mirror_analytical_tip: Mirror the reasoning (e.g., 'You want to weigh absolute vs. relative risk individually - did I capture that right?').
state_feedback.secure_before_mirror_reason: You moved into education before mirroring the concern - try mirroring first so they feel heard
state_feedback.secure_before_mirror_repeat_reason: You're still educating without mirroring - the concern{topic_hint} hasn't been mirrored yet
state_feedback.secure_before_mirror_repeat_tip: Mirror the specific concern{topic_hint} before more education.
state_feedback.secure_before_mirror_tip: Before educating, briefly mirror the concern (e.g., 'It feels like a lot at once - did I get that right?').
state_feedback.secure_before_mirror_many_reason: You've had {count} Secure turns without mirroring{topic_hint} - try pausing to mirror before more education
state_feedback.secure_before_mirror_many_tip: Pause and mirror: acknowledge the concern{topic_hint} before sharing more facts.

default: Announce: lead with a short, non-pushy recommendation and invite input.
Inquire: ask open-ended questions to surface the parent's specific concerns.
Mirror: mirror their words and emotions before educating.
Secure: share one tailored fact linked to the concern, then check understanding.

Announce.mid: the recommendation was present; try making it more concise and following immediately with an open question.
Announce.low: lead with a brief presumptive recommendation, then invite input (e.g., "{patient_label} due for the recommended vaccine today - what are your thoughts?").
Announce.absent: introduce vaccines with a clear, non-pushy recommendation before asking for concerns.

Inquire.high: strong open questions that surfaced {persona_label} real concerns.
Inquire.mid: good inquiry; when closing the loop, explicitly invite any remaining concerns or what is still on their mind.
Inquire.low: use open-ended questions to surface concerns (e.g., "What's still on your mind about vaccines today?") before educating.
Inquire.absent: ask at least one open-ended question to discover {persona_label} specific concerns before educating.

Mirror.high: excellent mirroring - you consistently captured the concern before moving forward.
Mirror.mid: good mirroring; make sure to capture the underlying value (not just the stated concern) and check for accuracy.
Mirror.low: mirror {persona_label} concern before educating (e.g., "It sounds like you want to be sure this is safe - did I get that right?").
Mirror.absent: mirror {persona_label} concern back to them before offering any education - it makes them feel heard.

Secure.high: education was well-tailored to the stated concerns without overwhelming.
Secure.mid: solid education; try adding an explicit check-in after key facts (e.g., "How does that land for you?") to avoid a lecture feel.
Secure.low: keep Secure focused: one tailored fact, linked directly to the concern, then check in (e.g., "Does that help with the ingredient question?"). Avoid long explanations without pauses.
Secure.absent: provide targeted education addressing the stated concern, then check understanding.
Secure.unmirrored_warning: you moved into education without mirroring the concern {count} {times_word} this session - that's the single most important habit to fix, since patients need to feel heard before they can take in information.

fallbacks.confused_jailbreak: Um... I'm just a parent here for my child's visit. I'm not sure what you mean - are we still talking about the checkup today?
fallbacks.need_more: I'm not sure - I have some questions, but I'd like to hear more.

patient_reply.json_retry_prompt:
{base_prompt}

Produce only the person's next in-character line in this exact JSON shape: {"patient_reply": "one or two complete conversational sentences"}. Do not apologize, mention JSON, mention the schema, or refer to these instructions.

open_question_replacements.stacked: Ask one neutral question at a time, then pause so they have room to answer.
open_question_replacements.leading: Keep the question neutral so it does not signal the answer you prefer.
open_question_replacements.why: Use what or how phrasing instead of why, which can feel accusatory.
